inspected: Reconstruction read: Section 2, printed pp.278--281, equations (2)--(6): lag moments, predetermined versus strictly exogenous regressors
Section 3: residual serial-correlation test and its estimation correction
PDF pp.2-5; serial-correlation discussion, equation2 moment restrictions, equations5-6 predetermined/exogenous variables
claims: Dynamic panel GMM requires serial-correlation and overidentification diagnostics.
Predetermined and endogenous regressors admit different lag-instrument sets after differencing.
First-order differenced-error correlation is expected under white-noise level innovations; second-order correlation probes moment validity.
sources.limits: Internal instruments need valid moments; instrument proliferation is a concern.

sources.title: Initial conditions and Blundell–Bond estimators
sources.version_status: Journal of Econometrics 234 (2023), 101--110; published PDF inspected
sources.local_path: docs/papers/Initial conditions and Blundell–Bond estimators Blundell(2023).pdf
inspected: Abstract and Section 1: dynamic panels with persistent economic series and motivation for system estimator
Section 2.3, pp.104--105: differenced moments, two-step weight and finite-sample variance correction
Section 2.4, p.106: weak instruments as persistence approaches unity and initial-condition alternatives
Sections 3.1--3.3, pp.107--109: E(delta y_i2 alpha_i)=0, decomposition around long-run mean, level instruments and weighting qualification
claims: System moments need additional initial-condition restrictions; two-step variance requires a finite-sample correction; persistence weakens differenced-panel instruments.
sources.limits: 2023 retrospective, not a replacement for the original 1998 paper; source-specific summary and no generic system-GMM validity claim.
